title: Windows Cisco Secure Endpoint Related Service Stopped
exclusions: Windows only, and only the Secure Endpoint, Orbital, and Immunet services listed. A French-language system writes `arrêté`; add the stopped string for other display languages.
evidence: Saved alert results with the host and services, plus the upgrade or maintenance ticket, or the incident record, for each host.

controlTest.positiveScenario: On a test host with the Secure Endpoint connector and Connector Protection disabled, stop the Cisco Secure Endpoint service from Services as an administrator. Windows writes Event 7036 with the service name and `stopped`, and the search returns one row for the host.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Stop and start an unrelated service such as Print Spooler on the same host. Event 7036 is written, but the service name is not in the list and the search returns no row.

dataSources: `index=wineventlog source=XmlWinEventLog:System EventCode=7036` from the Service Control Manager on Windows endpoints with the Secure Endpoint connector. In XML rendering `param1` is the service display name and `param2` the new state.
app: Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows ([Splunkbase 742](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/742)), Windows System event log.
spl:
index=wineventlog source="XmlWinEventLog:System" EventCode=7036
| rename param1 as display_name, param2 as status
| search display_name IN ("Cisco AMP Orbital", "*Cisco Secure Endpoint*", "*Cisco Security Connector Monitoring*", "CiscoSAM", "CiscoAMPHeurDriver", "CiscoAMPELAMDriver", "CiscoAMPCEFWDriver", "ImmunetNetworkMonitorDriver", "ImmunetProtectDriver", "ImmunetSelfProtectDriver") status IN ("stopped", "arrêté")
| stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(display_name) as services by dest
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
description: Finds Windows Service Control Manager events (7036) reporting that a Cisco Secure Endpoint, Orbital, or Immunet service or driver entered the stopped state, grouped by host with the list of services stopped.
value: Ransomware and hands-on attackers stop endpoint protection before they act. Event 7036 is written by Windows itself, so it still shows the stop even when the attacker used a method other than the connector's own tool.
implementation: Collect the Windows System event log in XML from endpoints with the Secure Endpoint connector into `index=wineventlog`. Schedule every 15 minutes and alert on every host, excluding planned upgrade windows.
visualization: Alert table: firstTime, lastTime, dest, services, count. Supporting panel: 30-day count of connector service stops by host (bar chart).

references.title: Cisco Secure Endpoint: command-line switches for the Windows connector

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Connector upgrades** — upgrading the connector stops and restarts its services. The stop is followed by a running event within minutes; check for the matching restart.

2. **Shutdown and reboot** — services stop during a normal shutdown. Correlate with Event 1074 or 6006 on the same host.

**Suppression:** drop hosts where a 7036 running event for the same service follows within 10 minutes, and use a maintenance-window lookup for upgrades.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (Splunkbase 742) on the search heads and on the Universal Forwarders of the Windows endpoints.
• An index for Windows event logs (this page uses `index=wineventlog`) and a role with `srchIndexesAllowed` on it for the SOC.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
• In the forwarder's inputs.conf enable `[WinEventLog://System]` with `renderXml = true` and `index = wineventlog`; events arrive as `sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog` with `source=XmlWinEventLog:System`.
• Event 7036 is written by the Service Control Manager whenever a service changes state; with XML rendering the add-on extracts `param1` (display name) and `param2` (state).
• Check the data this search needs: run `index=wineventlog source="XmlWinEventLog:System" EventCode=7036 param1="*Cisco*" | stats count by param1 param2` over 7 days.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=wineventlog source="XmlWinEventLog:System" EventCode=7036
| rename param1 as display_name, param2 as status
| search display_name IN ("Cisco AMP Orbital", "*Cisco Secure Endpoint*", "*Cisco Security Connector Monitoring*", "CiscoSAM", "CiscoAMPHeurDriver", "CiscoAMPELAMDriver", "CiscoAMPCEFWDriver", "ImmunetNetworkMonitorDriver", "ImmunetProtectDriver", "ImmunetSelfProtectDriver") status IN ("stopped", "arrêté")
| stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(display_name) as services by dest
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
```

Understanding this SPL
• The first line limits the search to service state changes in the System log.
• `rename` gives `param1` and `param2` readable names; the `search` list covers the connector, Orbital, and the Immunet drivers.
• `status IN ("stopped", "arrêté")` covers English and French display languages; add others you run.
• `stats` per host lists every connector service stopped in the window.

Step 3 — Validate
• Compare with the Secure Endpoint console (Management > Computers) for the host: the connector should show as not reporting or with a fault after the alert time.
• Confirm in Event Viewer on the host (Windows Logs > System, source Service Control Manager, Event 7036) that the stop exists.
• Run `index=wineventlog source="XmlWinEventLog:System" | timechart span=1h count` over 7 days to confirm the System log is arriving continuously.

Step 4 — Operationalize
• Schedule every 15 minutes over the last 20 minutes and throttle on `dest` for 1 hour.
• Route to the SOC with the matching restart check: if the service did not come back within 10 minutes and there is no ticket, isolate the host.
• Enable Connector Protection in the Secure Endpoint policy so the services cannot be stopped without a password.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting
• No 7036 events with `param1`: the forwarder collects `WinEventLog:System` without XML, so `param1` and `param2` do not exist. Set `renderXml = true` or rewrite the search on `Message`.
• Rows for every reboot: add the restart-suppression from the Known false positives section.
• Service names do not match: connector versions rename services. Run the Step 1 check and update the list.
grandmaExplanation: We alert when the security software on a Windows computer is switched off, because attackers do that right before they do damage.
